Unde etiam à Pontificiis Articulus hic, dictis verbis constans, simpliciter admissus fertur ab Historiographis Augustanae Confessionis omnibus. Quod ad posteriorem verò mutationem attinet, ignotum esse haud potest, & similem, imò prolixiorem multò improbationem omissam deprehendi in Augustanae Confessionis invariatae Exemplaribus Chytraei & Caelestini, inter se collatis, quoad Articulum XIII. & XVIII. (Quae tamen Omissio nihil prohibuit, quò minus ab Invariatae Confessionis Theologis utrumque Exemplar pro genuino habitum semper sit, hodièque habeatur.) & in plurimis Articulis e.g. in 3. 4. 6. 7. 11. 14. 18. 19. 20. 21. ne a prima quidem Aug. Confessionis adornatione improbationem contrariorum adjectam, nihilominus subaudiendam fuisse.
english: As for the other change — or rather the omission in the Variata of And they reject those who teach otherwise — we admit those exact words are not read there.
Yet in every article of any confession the same sense, or something like it, must be understood: whoever positively confesses a point always denies and rejects what stands against it.
So the omission is only an avoidance of tautology; it can introduce no substantial mutation.

I pass over this further note on the prior change: in the prototype exemplar of the Invariata as the German plainly shows, and Dorsche does not deny it page 183, the article was expressed thus — Concerning the Lord's Supper they confess that the body and blood of Christ are truly present under the species of bread and wine — which at that time could easily smell of pontifical transubstantiation by itself.
Hence the historiographers of the Augsburg Confession report that the pontificals simply admitted this article in those words.

And as for the later omission, it is no secret that a similar — indeed much longer — rejection is missing in the Invariata exemplars of Chytraeus and Caelestinus when Article XIII and XVIII are compared; yet that omission never kept Invariata theologians from treating either exemplar as genuine then or now.
In many articles besides — 3, 4, 6, 7, 11, 14, 18, 19, 20, 21 — no rejection of contrary teaching was added even at the Confession's first framing, and yet it was still to be heard as implied.

source_text: POSTERIUS verò à nobis probandum, scil. mutationem praesertim priorem, Calvinianae Sententiae nullâ ex parte magis favere, quam ipse Articulus invariatus ei favet, sic illucescit: Quia cumprimis Calvinus, Reformatorum Doctoribus annumeratus, & cum Calvino Reformatae Ecclesiae omnes, & veram praesentiam, & veram distributionem Corporis & Sanguinis Christi, in S. Coena admittunt, non minùs quam veram exhibitionem, istasque propter hanc, quam nusquam non inculcant seriò, Signa Sacramentalia, non nude Significantia, sed & Exhibentia, confessi. Justas: At, sub Variatae Confessionis verbis, quibus Corpus & Sanguis Christi, nudè exhiberi, non autem adesse & distribui dicuntur, occultare facilius Calvinianos sententiam suam de Spirituali Corporis & Sanguinis Christi exhibitione posse, ut dum exhiberi ista dicunt verè, Spiritualiter duntaxat exhiberi doceant?
english: The second point we must prove — that the change, especially the prior one, favors the Calvinian sense no more than the unvaried article itself does — comes clear this way.

Calvin, counted among the Reformed doctors, and with him all the Reformed churches, admit a true presence and a true distribution of Christ's body and blood in the holy Supper, no less than a true exhibition.
And because of that exhibition, which they never fail to press, they confess the sacramental signs to be not bare signs only, but also exhibiting signs.

Fair enough. But the charge runs: under the Variata's words, where body and blood are said only to be exhibited, not to be present and distributed, Calvinists can more easily hide a merely spiritual exhibition — saying truly exhibited while teaching exhibited only spiritually.

source_text: Resp. (1.) Idem facere posse Calvinianos in verbis Invariatae Confessionis, ut dum dicunt: Corpus & Sanguinem Christi verè adesse & distribui, illa spiritualiter tantum adesse & distribui intelligant. (2.) Etiam invariatae solius Confessores, Spiritualem praesentiam pariter atque distributionem, haud magis quàm Exhibitionem ac Manducationem Spiritualem, inficiari, praesertim cum & suam Corporalem praesentiam, Distributionem, Manducationem & Exhibitionem, hyperphysicas nihilominus & Supernaturales inculcent esse. (3.) Non nudam Spiritualem praesentiam, Distributionem & Exhibitionem Corporis & Sanguinis Christi docere Reformatos, sed & Sacramentalem, licèt non Corporalem, utpote in neutra Confessione Augustana, nec in priori magis, quàm posteriori, edoctam.
english: Answer. First, they can do the same with the Invariata's words: while it says Christ's body and blood are truly present and distributed, they may take that as only spiritual presence and distribution.

Second, even confessors of the Invariata alone do not deny spiritual presence and distribution any more than spiritual exhibition and eating — especially since they also insist that their own corporal presence, distribution, eating, and exhibition are nonetheless hyperphysical and supernatural.

Third, the Reformed do not teach a naked spiritual presence, distribution, and exhibition of Christ's body and blood, but a sacramental one as well — though not a corporal one, which neither Augsburg Confession teaches, earlier or later.

source_text:
§. IX.
Dorschei Canones reliqui, quibus Confessionem Philippicam, privata tantum Auctoritate, non etiam publica Subsequente factam, quin, publicâ Auctoritate improbatam rejectamque, esse, innuit,
english: §. IX. Dorsche's remaining canons hint that the Philippica Confession rested on private authority alone — not on later public authority — and was even condemned and rejected by public authority.

source_text: praeterquam quòd, ab Auctoribus supra allegatis, sigillatim Joh. Crocio Comm. Cap. LVI. pag. 746. ab ipso etiam Mentzero Lutherano, non agnoscuntur,
english: Besides, the authors already cited do not own those canons — least of all John Crocius (Commentary, ch. 56, p. 746), and not even Mentzer the Lutheran.

source_text: ita ex ipso Dorscheo falsitatis arguuntur, per jam tum retrò memoratarum ad Ferdinandum I. Imperatorem, à Statibus Imperii datarum & a Dorscheo pagina 20. integra in vernacula nostra lingua recensitarum literarum, verba sequentia:
english: So Dorsche himself convicts them of falsehood: the letter already named — from the Imperial Estates to Emperor Ferdinand I — which he prints in full in our vernacular at page 20, runs as follows:

source_text: Gleichergestalt wollen wir auch hiemit die Apologi/ so durch unsere Vorfahren/ und zum theil uns /auf gemeltem Reichs Tag zu Augspurg/ überreichet / aber man nicht hat annehmen wollen/wie die selbige hernach zu Wittenberg gedruckt/und auf gedachtem Colloquio zu Wormbs A. 1540. neben obberührten verbesserten Confession übergeben / ausdrucklich repetirt und uns darzu bekennt haben.
english: Likewise we hereby also hold the Apology which our ancestors — and partly we ourselves — presented at that Augsburg Diet, though it was not accepted; afterward it was printed at Wittenberg, and at the Worms Colloquy in 1540 it was delivered beside the improved Confession already named — expressly repeated, and we have confessed ourselves to it.

source_text: Wie denn auch gleicher gestalt unsere Meinung dahin gericht / daß wir andere der unsere Schrifften und repetirte Confessionen/ so der Kays: Maj. aufgehaltenen Reichs-Tagen und Colloquien/durch die Ständ/unserer Religion/zu weiterer Erklärung der beständigen und unwiederlegten Warheit / und Abwendung deren eine lange Zeit eingerissenen falschen Lehren und Mißbrauchen übergeben / und zum Theil publiciret/ hiemit nicht verwerffen / noch begeben / sondern dieselbe/im Verstand der heiligen Schrifft und ieko erneurter Augspurgischen Confession und Apologi gemäß/in alle Weg wollen vorbehalten haben. Da auch unser Gegentheil etliche Articul oder Wörter in dieser Augspurgischen Confession und Apologi / welche zum Anfang dieser hochnothwendigen / unvermeidentlichen Veränderung / zum Theil/ auch nach Art und Gebrauch der Teutschen Sprachen zu reden / zum glimpfligsten gestellt / und sonderlich da vom H. Sacrament und Messe / auch von der Römischen Kirchen gemelt wird / zu ihrem Vortheil und dahin deuten oder ziehen wolten / als wenn wir auch mit ihren abgöttischen Lehren und Ceremonien/in denen sich gleichwol nachgehends allerhand Christliche Aenderungen zugetragen / der Päpstischen Kirchen /und sonderlich dem Greuel der transubstantiation , der Päpstischen Meß / und was dem anhängig / einig/ so erklären wir uns hiemit abermal / daß es die Meinung gar nicht hat / &c.
english: In the same way our mind is this: we do not reject or give up our other writings and repeated Confessions — those the Estates of our religion handed in at Imperial Diets and colloquies under His Majesty, partly published, to explain the standing, unrefuted truth and to drive out long-settled false teaching and abuse.
We mean to keep them in every way in the sense of holy Scripture and of the now-renewed Augsburg Confession and Apology.

And when our opponents twist some early, mild articles or words in that Confession and Apology — set gently, partly in German speech-habit, especially where the holy Sacrament, the Mass, and the Roman Church are named — as if we agreed with their idolatrous papal teachings and ceremonies (in which Christian changes later came anyway), and above all with the horror of transubstantiation, the papal Mass, and what hangs on it: we declare again that this is not our meaning at all.

source_text: & post. Hinwiderum aber ist unser Meinung und Fürsatz gar nicht/ daß wir in unsern Landen/ Gebieten / Kirchen / und Schulen einige andere Lehr / denn die / wie obgemelt/ in der heiligen göttlichen Schrifft gegründet/und der Augspurgischen Confession und Apologi in ihrem rechten Verstand gemäß / dulden oder vertheidigen/ sondern uns allein zu der erkanten Warheit bekennen/ und nichts / so derselben entgegen/ einreissen lassen / oder gestatten wollen. &c. Confer. Historiam Conventus Nauenburgici hôc ipso anno in vernacula nostra denuo recensitam a Dn. D. Hönnio, Consiliario Saxonico Ducali ac Secretario intimo pag. 103. 105. 106. 107.
english: And afterward: on the contrary, it is not our mind or purpose to tolerate or defend in our lands, territories, churches, and schools any teaching other than what is grounded, as said above, in holy Scripture and fits the Augsburg Confession and Apology in their right sense.
We mean to confess the known truth alone, and to let nothing against it break in or be allowed.
Compare the History of the Naumburg Convention, reviewed again this very year in our vernacular by Dr. Hoennius, Ducal Saxon councillor and intimate secretary (pp. 103, 105, 106, 107).
